Foundation examination: Volumes1–4Economics core examination

Assessment standard

Demonstrate mastery

Progress is earned through correct reasoning, transfer to unfamiliar problems, credible empirical analysis, and clear explanation. Studying time and page counts are inputs; they do not establish competence.

Every chapter

Complete at least eight original exercises (ten in graduate technical chapters), reconstruct the worked examples, explain a mechanism without notes, and answer a later retention question. Determinate problems have complete solutions. Open questions have evaluation criteria and may admit several defensible answers.

Every volume

Complete a prerequisite diagnostic, cumulative examination, distinct reassessment form, integrative project, oral explanation, and delayed retention check. Projects specify inputs, outputs, assumptions, uncertainty, reproducibility and scoring. Volume-specific examination and project materials will appear when their packages are written.

Advancement criteria

Our proposed default for numerical/conceptual exams is at least 85% overall with no essential domain below 75%, plus a transfer problem and teach-back. These are design choices for this library, not university requirements. Critical errors in identification, units, budget balance, risk interpretation or integrity require correction regardless of the total.

Graduate and research assessment

Graduate work adds proofs, derivations, model critique, empirical identification and numerical diagnostics. The research portfolio includes replication, referee reports, a proposal, original work and an oral defense. Qualified researchers must evaluate its contribution and correctness; the book cannot award that judgment automatically.

Teaching and leadership

A teaching portfolio contains undergraduate and graduate syllabi, lessons, assessments, grading criteria, observed teaching and research-supervision plans. A leadership portfolio contains strategy, budgets, decision rights, hiring and incentives, risk and crisis decisions, and a retrospective on real responsibility. Independent observation and real experience are essential.

Editorial acceptance

A chapter package is accepted only after its instruction, worked examples, exercises, solutions, sources and review record satisfy the production contract. Source-link checks, numerical checks and subject-matter review are recorded separately. Draft is a transparent production state, not a mastery credential.

Cumulative examinations and portfolios

Each assessment combines its prerequisite volumes. Planned entries specify future work; available links open written material.

Foundation examination: Volumes1–4 Author-reviewed

Integrate economic and financial reasoning, mathematical justification, uncertainty and reproducible empirical analysis.

Two distinct written forms, original basic data-analysis practical with documented inputs/benchmark, complete solutions and rubrics, oral transfer and remediation.

Prerequisites: v01, v02, v03, v04

Economics core examination Author-reviewed

Connect microeconomic choices and strategic interaction to macroeconomic and international mechanisms.

Cumulative theoretical and applied problems, complete solutions/rubrics and reassessment.

Prerequisites: v01, v02, v03, v04, v05, v06

Finance core examination Planned

Integrate accounting, valuation, investments, derivatives and financial-institution risk.

Valuation, portfolio and institutional-risk cases with solutions, reproducible inputs and reassessment.

Prerequisites: v07, v08, v09, v10, v11

Graduate qualifying sequence Planned

Defend graduate econometric, microeconomic and macro-finance derivations and research reasoning.

Separate econometrics, micro theory and macro-finance exams with distinct reassessment forms, complete solutions and oral defense rubrics.

Prerequisites: v12, v13, v14

Integrated policy and investment case Planned

Connect mechanism, identification, valuation, distribution and institutional feasibility.

Documented integrated case, scenario/model/data inputs, decision memo, benchmark and argument-specific evaluation.

Prerequisites: v05, v06, v08, v11, v12, v15

Research portfolio Planned

Produce and defend a scoped original contribution with reproducible evidence.

Replication package, two referee reports, proposal, original paper and oral-defense protocol requiring independent expert evaluation.

Prerequisites: v12, v13, v14, v15, v16

Teaching portfolio Planned

Design, teach and assess coherent undergraduate and graduate material.

Syllabi, sample lessons, assessments/rubrics, observed-teaching protocol and supervision plan requiring human observation.

Prerequisites: v16, v17

Leadership portfolio Planned

Defend strategy, resources, governance and crisis decisions and reflect on real responsibility.

Strategy memo, budget, governance map, hiring/incentive plan, crisis exercise and observed real-responsibility retrospective.

Prerequisites: v07, v08, v11, v16, v17, v18
